overview: This House resolution marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. It offers sympathy to the victims and their families, and honors the troops, civilian personnel, first responders, and volunteers who risked their lives and health. It thanks other nations that have stood with the United States against terrorism and commends the military and intelligence personnel involved in the operation that killed Osama bin Laden, the leader of the group behind the attacks. The House recommits to fighting terrorism and to giving the military, intelligence agencies, and law enforcement the resources to do so, and it adjourns for the day out of respect for the victims. It does not by itself change any law or spending. As of September 10, 2026, the House had adopted it.
for: Supporters say a formal statement on the 25th anniversary honors the victims and those who served, and restates the country's resolve against terrorism.
against: Critics say the resolution is largely symbolic, and its broad promise of resources for counterterrorism does not itself set any policy or spending.
